implementation_notes: gMock cannot intercept an existing object, so the C++ spy is a mock class whose default action delegates to the real implementation: declare the interface, subclass it with MOCK_METHOD, and wire the delegation via ON_CALL(*this, DoThis).WillByDefault([this](int n) { return real_.DoThis(n); }) so calls execute the genuine code while EXPECT_CALL records which interactions happened. What replaces the classic spy object is a mock with a delegating default action plus call assertions; when the real object is final or the method non-virtual, extract an interface (or wrap it) rather than reaching for interception tricks.
pitfalls: Delegation must be installed before any custom ON_CALL/EXPECT_CALL overrides (the cookbook's ordering rule); a later WillByDefault silently replaces the forwarding.
gMock records only what an EXPECT_CALL declared interest in; without one the call is still forwarded but not asserted, and uninteresting calls on a NaggyMock print warnings.
The mock is a different type from the real object, so it cannot be passed where the concrete class is required - keep the seam at an interface.
